games.name: Corner Cutters
games.shortDescription: Top-down racing for people who love a good fight for a corner. AI drivers defend and make mistakes. Tyres wear and grip best when warm. Rubber builds up on the line, and in changing weather the track dries where the cars drive. Best played with a controller. Race a season or go online.
games.aboutText:
Corner Cutters is top-down racing for people who love a good fight for a corner. Up to twenty cars on the grid, and nobody gives one up for free.

Drivers who fight back

They race for real: they look for gaps, defend their place and try the inside when you leave room. Sometimes they get it wrong. Push someone off or cut a corner, and the stewards will notice.

Best played with a controller

The triggers give you full control of the throttle and the brake, and the rumble tells you what the tyres are doing. You feel a wheel lock under braking, the tail start to slide, the kerbs, the grass, a worn tyre and a flat one. In another car's slipstream, the pad shakes in the turbulent air. You can also drive with a keyboard, and every menu works with a controller.

Tyres and pit stops

Soft, medium, hard, intermediate and wet. Your tyres wear out and need the right temperature to grip. You choose when to pit, and the crew does the rest: new tyres, and repairs if you need them.

Dynamic track

With changing weather on, rain can start in the middle of a race, and stop again. When it stops, every car's tyres push the water off the track, so a dry line appears where the cars actually drive, with more grip than the wet track beside it. Stay out on wets, or gamble on slicks?

In a dry race, the track starts clean. Every car leaves rubber where it drives, most of all in the corners where the tyres work hard. Lap by lap the line gets darker and gives a little more grip, so you can get on the power earlier. The AI drivers feel it too.

Three classes of car

- Formula: open-wheel cars, the fastest. A flap on the rear wing opens on the straights.

- GT: heavy cars, with the engine in the front, the middle or the back. They slide more.

- Roadster: small cars with little power. If you brake too much, it takes a long time to get your speed back.

Eleven circuits

Race through a harbour, a neon city at night, a desert canyon, sand dunes by the sea and a bowl with steep banked corners. Seen from above, one circuit is shaped like a raven. And one is a figure of eight that crosses itself on a bridge, because why not.

Championships

Pick your circuits and race a season of 2 to 20 rounds, with a team-mate and a teams' title to fight for. Finish on the podium and there's champagne.

Online

Host a room on Steam or on your local network for up to twenty people, and fill the empty places with AI drivers if you like. Every room has text chat and can run its own championship. On Steam you can turn on voice chat: you hear the drivers near you on track, and a team-mate over the radio.

Time trials

Set your best lap alone on any circuit, and race against your own ghost to find the last tenth.

Good to know

- Replays: watch your races back and follow any car you like.

- Liveries: paint your car in your own colours, with 18 patterns, some earned with achievements.

- Your own music: music is personal. Turn the game's music off, or drop your own songs in a folder and they play in the menus and the races.

- Camera: set it as close or as far as you like, also during a race, and choose whether it zooms out as you go faster.

- Steering wheels are not supported, and the game is in English.

Win something. Anything.

A note from me

Hi, I'm Ferdi! I've been making games for over twenty years, and I love motorsport. Watching a race, sim racing, a day of karting with friends: for me, nothing beats a good fight for a corner. That's what I wanted in a game, so I made Corner Cutters: easy to pick up, with racing that's real. I've driven thousands of laps on these circuits during development, and I'm still finding faster lines. If something feels off, or you just want to say hi, let me know. I read everything.

I hope you have as much fun racing it as I do.

games.name: Lost Bitcoin
games.shortDescription: Lost Bitcoin is a digging and automation game set in a gigantic junkyard. Collect scrap, burn it for coins, buy upgrades and build a factory that works for you. Crack crates and safes, and check every USB stick to find your lost Bitcoin wallet.
games.aboutText:
Somewhere beneath this gigantic junkyard lies your Bitcoin USB stick. Find the right one among many.

1. Collect and Burn

Pull scrap out, carry it to the furnace and throw it in. Every piece pays coins. The deeper you dig, the more it pays.

2. Buy Upgrades

More than 60 upgrades in a skill tree, and more are planned.

3. Collect More and Burn More

Suck up a whole tank of scrap and shoot it into the furnace. And there are many more ways to farm more efficiently and progress faster.

4. Build a Factory

Up on the deck you build a factory of your own. Cranes lift scrap out, belts and sorting gates send it on, and machines turn it into rubber ducks, piggy banks, arcade machines and little robots. It earns money while you dig.

5. Check USB Sticks and Find Treasures

USB sticks are everywhere, and they all look the same. Only the computer on the platform tells you what is on one. Along the way you find crates, safes, golden pieces and an entire sailing ship buried under the scrap. Cut your way in. Maybe you'll find your Bitcoins and get rich.

6. Wishlist This Game

Wishlist Lost Bitcoin so you don’t miss the release.

games.aboutText:
Escape the Walls is an incremental game, where you start with only your fists and punch your way through walls

Punch. Upgrade. Fight Enemies. Go deeper each time

Danger hides behind every wall

The only way is forward

Try to Escape the Walls!

games.name: SHRED A BILLION
games.shortDescription: SHRED A BILLION is a first-person incremental game about a mountain of money! Grab bills by hand, scoop them with a bucket, level up and feed a billion dollars to the shredder. Only 999,999,999 bills left to go!
games.aboutText:
One billion dollars. One shredder. You.

A gigantic bank vault is buried under money up to the ceiling — mountains of bills and bundles. Your job is simple and glorious: dig through all that wealth and feed it to the shredder. Every bill pays out, every upgrade makes you faster, and the mountain keeps shrinking.

Grab, scoop, suck it up

Start with your bare hands: grab bills one by one and carry them to the shredder. Then go bigger: a bucket, a shovel and a powerful vacuum that pulls money in a swirling vortex. When your hands get tired, launch drones — they mine and haul the cash without you.

Upgrades you can't put down

- Over 100 upgrades for your tools, the shredder and your drones

- A skill tree with branches for your play style

- Boosts, relics and golden banknotes for the long run

- Numbers climb from your first dollars to trillions — and beyond

A secret at the bottom of the vault

The vault goes five levels deep. The deeper you dig, the bigger the bills. Shred every last bill, pick up the golden key and open the massive door at the bottom. What's behind it? Find out for yourself.

Better together

Play solo or invite up to three friends to online co-op. Shared progress, one shared mountain of money, voice and text chat — dig together, argue about who buys the next upgrade, and shred a billion as a team.

Features

- A cozy first-person incremental game

- Exactly one billion banknotes in the vault, counted down to the very last one

- Online co-op for up to 4 players with voice chat

- Drone automation — up to 16 drones dig and haul the cash on their own

- Five signature moves: ARMFUL, HEAVE, GROUND POUND, OVERLOAD and RALLY

- The jetpack lifts you out of any pit

- Customize your thief and find hats in buried chests

- A Steam leaderboard for the fastest vault clear, solo and in co-op

- 100 Steam achievements

- Fully localized into 30 languages

games.name: Tidy Up Christmas Shop
games.shortDescription: 5,434 Christmas items are scattered across the shop. Put them back where they belong and enjoy the wonderful order. No timer, no stress. Upgrade your skills with the candy you earn and arrange colourful, twinkling Christmas items on the shelves of a huge two-storey shop as you like. Merry Christmas!
games.aboutText:
Tomorrow is opening day for a magical Christmas shop, but inside it looks like a battlefield. Twinkling baubles, sparkling bells, crystal ornaments, ribboned gift boxes and thousands more are scattered everywhere. If every item makes it back to its own shelf, the shop's magic will return.

Pick up the items on the floor and put them in the right category. You can carry a stack of up to eight items in your hands.

Put an item on the right shelf and it glows green. Yellow means another kind has slipped into that compartment; red means the item is on the wrong shelf.

Every corner of this huge, magical two-storey shop has been lovingly prepared to be decked out with twinkling decorations.

And don't forget to ring the bell on the counter. It might just come in handy.

- 5,434 items, 499 kinds, 40 categories

- No timer, no penalties: play at your own pace

- Twinkling, enchanting, handcrafted 3D Christmas ornaments

- A snowy night, warm lights and a giant fir tree

games.name: Shellcrushers
games.shortDescription: Shellcrushers is a stylized horde tower defense game: tens of thousands of roaches pour in at once, and you meet them with six turrets, RPG-deep upgrade trees and procedurally generated maps, so no two fights play the same.
games.aboutText:
Shellcrushers is a stylized tower defense game about a roach swarm the size of a river, turrets you build up like RPG characters, and maps that are never the same twice.

The Shellcrushers are an elite squad of small aliens who already lost their home world to the swarm. Now the roaches on Earth are waking up, and the Extermination Service sends crews in before the humans notice. Clear the site, collect the biomass, file the report in triplicate. The end of the world is no excuse to skip the paperwork.

Before the wave, place every turret by hand: turn its firing sector, pull it closer or push it farther, and a drop pod brings it down.

Tens of thousands of roaches flow toward your base like a river. Every one that slips through costs you.

A toothpick machine gun, a cannon, a flamethrower, a tesla coil, a railgun and a rocket launcher. Each turret picks one of its four ascendancies, and that choice changes how it fights: shells that punch through a whole line, rockets that leave a poison cloud, toothpicks that set the crowd on fire. The sets differ from turret to turret, drawn from five elements: physical, fire, ice, poison and lightning.

You fire too: click anywhere on the map and the HQ howitzer hits that spot.

At level 5 every turret unlocks its own ability. You aim it, and all turrets of that type fire together. In Coordinate Salvo, for example, every rocket launcher hits the point you pick, however far away it stands.

Three campaigns of five maps each: a kitchen, a restaurant and a warehouse. A job board of procedurally generated maps in five tiers, with skull modifiers to make them harder. And the sewers: 100 levels down, each one harder than the last. The task board keeps three tasks open and brings new ones every 30 minutes.

Every turret has its own big tree of upgrades with branches and builds to plan. Between runs, spend what you scrape off the roaches and shape each turret your way. On the toothpick machine gun alone, one build chases crits and ricochets, another lets the barrel heat up so every shot hits harder.

Each turret's own tree has about 300 nodes. Masteries let you take one rule out of several, and sockets hold modules: items with random properties, each rolled in one of five tiers. Legendary modules bring rules of their own. Modules drop in battle.

Elements react to each other. Ice on a burning roach puts the fire out and stuns it, lightning on a poisoned roach jumps to one more, and a heavy hit shatters a frozen roach into shards that cut its neighbours. Sixteen reactions in all. What's inside

- Six turrets , each with its own upgrade tree of about 300 nodes and four ascendancies

- Masteries and modules : rules to pick in the tree and items with random properties for its sockets

- 16 elemental reactions

- Three campaigns of five maps: a kitchen, a restaurant and a warehouse

- A job board of procedurally generated maps in five tiers, with skull modifiers

- The sewers : 100 levels down, each harder than the last

- A task board with new tasks every 30 minutes

- 73 Steam achievements and a leaderboard

- 15 languages
